name: David A. Varderpool
fact: The 1994 Talisman prints a Sigma Nu sophomore from Danville called Dave Vanderpool at p. 70, and Vanderpool, Dave, 70 is the only entry of anything like that surname in the index of either digitised volume. Varderpool is not a surname; Vanderpool is, and r for n is the commonest scanning slip there is. This is very probably the same man, but one letter is not a proof, so no portrait has been filed. His cell is the fourth of the third row on p. 70, counting the fifteen names down the left column five to a row, and it is staged unfiled as _unmatched-1994-95-dave-vanderpool.jpg.

name: Edward "Eddie" Myers
fact: NO USABLE FACE. The 1993 Talisman index reads "Myers, Edward 204" and that is his only appearance in either digitised volume (the 1994 volume names no Myers at all). Page 204 is the Student Government Association group photograph. It cannot be read positionally. The caption prints rows of six, eight and seven, twenty-one people; the printed FIRST row of six resolves perfectly, the figures running man, woman, man, woman, man, woman exactly as Donnie Miller, Jennifer Raffaelli, Jeremy Sublett, Susan Mitchell, Joe Rains, Cindy Hayes do. The other two rows do not. The group stands staggered on risers in four or five height bands rather than three, the topmost band holds eight figures where the printed third row has seven, and two of those eight are women where the third row's names are six men and Kibby Rose. An older grey-haired man stands in the middle of the top band who is very likely a faculty adviser and is not in the caption at all. Myers is first in the printed third row, so a mis-set row costs the identification outright. Two earlier researchers measured this same photograph independently and both put the faces at about eighteen pixels; measured again at native resolution here, the page is 864 pixels wide, the photograph 388 pixels wide, and a face runs about thirty pixels. No crop was cut.

name: Horace Johnson
fact: CONFIRMS THE STANDING REFUSAL, from a second and independent source. _do-not-use.json refuses every Herald photograph of a Horace Johnson on the ground that the paper's Horace Johnson is the campus police chief. The 1993 Talisman settles it the same way: its back index carries exactly one entry, "Johnson, Horace Jr. 78", and p. 78 is a FACULTY AND STAFF portrait page where the line beside the portrait reads Horace Johnson Jr., Public Safety Director. There is no student of that name anywhere in the 1993 or 1994 volume. So a portrait of a Horace Johnson does exist and is easy to find, and it is the wrong man. Do not file it.

name: Jason Young
fact: IDENTITY SETTLED, and a portrait is now filed. The Herald of 6 April 1995 profiles him as a presidential candidate with a labelled studio portrait, which is the frame now published. Two earlier-looking leads resolve against it. The Herald of 24 August 1993, p. 7, captions a cheerleading photograph "Hawesville junior Jason Young lifts Jennifer Wells ... Both are cheerleaders for football and men's basketball": that IS the same man, because the 1995 profile says he "was a Western cheerleader for three years" and calls him a Hawesville senior. It is refused anyway, on two grounds: the caption names one man and the frame shows two, a lifter and a spotter, with no positions given; and the likelier face is shot from below with the chin up and blown out white against black. The 1993 and 1994 Talisman indexes carry no Jason Young at all.

name: Edward "Eddie" Myers
fact: SOURCED FACT, no photograph. The Herald's report of the SGA election of 20 April 1993 names him among the winners: "Eddie Myers, a Hendersonville, Tenn., sophomore, junior class president", elected unopposed. That places him a year earlier than the archive's record of him and gives his home town and class, which is what makes it possible to test any later frame against him: a sophomore in 1992-93 is a senior in 1994-95, the year the archive records him chairing the Student Athletic Committee. The page carries a portrait of the new president Donald Smith and of nobody else.

name: David Bastin
fact: TRAP FOR THE NEXT PASS: there are two unrelated Bastins in the 1990s Herald and neither is straightforwardly this officer. MARTIN BASTIN is a Stanford, Ky. junior and a Persian Gulf veteran, photographed giving plasma in the Herald of 28 September 1993, p. 11, and carrying a class portrait in the 1993 Talisman index; he is far too early and is a different man. MATT BASTIN is a Shelbyville student, freshman in spring 1997 and Academic Affairs chair by autumn 1997, quoted in the Herald more than seventy times across 1997 and 1998; the 1997 dean's list prints him as "Matthew David Bastin", which is why he is very probably the David Bastin the archive's roll call of 3 December 1996 records. That is one letter of inference, not a proof, and no photograph of Matt Bastin was found in the 1997 or 1998 Heralds. Do not attach the Martin Bastin plasma frame or portrait to this officer.

name: Amy Braden
fact: A FRAME EXISTS AND IS REFUSED. The Herald of 27 February 1996, p. 1, runs a dramatic front-page photograph captioned "All the world's a stage: In front of Gordon Wilson Hall yesterday, Bowling Green freshman Helen Yeoman, Bowling Green sophomore Regina Johnson, Florence freshman Amy Braden, Louisville freshman Missy Payne and Louisville sophomore Heidi Stephenson rehearse the play 'The Five Chinese Brothers' for their Basic Techniques of Acting class" (Mandy Lunn/Herald). Five names, five women, and the caption gives no positions, so there is no sex or order test to run: it identifies nobody. The frame itself would fail anyway. It is a low-angle theatrical shot in which one figure in a white robe fills most of the picture with her head thrown back and her mouth open, and the others are behind her with hands over their faces or in deep shadow. A Florence freshman in February 1996 would be a sophomore in 1996-97, which fits the officer, but that is the only thing that does.

name: Steven Graham
fact: A FRAME EXISTS, IS CORRECTLY LABELLED, AND HAS NO FACE IN IT. The Herald's People Poll of 12 September 1996, p. 4, runs five mugshots in a row, each with its quotation and then its name set in bold directly beneath its own frame, and the leftmost reads "Steven Graham, Guthrie freshman". The identification of the FRAME is therefore sound. Two things stop it. First, the halftone is crushed: measured at the scan's native resolution the face is 52 per cent of pixels below tone 60, the whole head reads as one black shape and the only feature that survives is the line of the teeth; a level stretch between the 1st and 60th percentiles recovers nothing, exactly as with the refused Anne Guillory frame. Second, the PERSON is not proved. Nothing in the caption ties this student to student government; all the archive has is a Guthrie freshman of that name in the same academic year as a Steven Graham who answered a roll call on 3 December 1996. Recorded rather than filed so that a later pass with a better scan can weigh it.

name: John W. Taylor
fact: IDENTIFIED IN THE HERALD, NEVER PHOTOGRAPHED, AND THE ONLY COVERAGE OF HIM IS A DISCIPLINARY CASE. An editor's note in the Herald of 28 February 1995, p. 4, states that "John Taylor is the 33-year-old president of Students Over Traditional Age and an SGA representative", which is a contemporaneous confirmation of the Non-Traditional Rep the archive records for 1994-95 and gives his age. The note was printed under a reader's letter arguing that a student called John Taylor should not have lost his place over an alleged possession of marijuana; the letter is the correspondence the Herald ran about a committee decision, it names no outcome, and the archive's own rules bar using a frame tied to a censure even if one existed. None exists here: the page carries a cartoon and a People Poll of four other students and no photograph of him. He is also absent from the 1991-1994 Talisman indexes.
